title: The Bees, the Drones and the Wasp
text:
Some bees had built their honeycombs high in an oak tree. A group of lazy drones came along and claimed the combs were theirs. The bees protested, and since neither side would give way, the case was brought before a judge: the wasp.

The wasp knew both kinds of creature well, and she saw at once that they looked much alike and buzzed with the same color and sound. Appearances would not decide this. So she proposed a simple test. Each side should take an empty hive and build new combs and fill them with honey. Then she would compare the shape of the cells and the taste of the honey with what was in the oak, and the true makers would be obvious.

The bees agreed immediately. The drones refused. They had no intention of building anything, because they could not.

That refusal was enough for the wasp. She gave her verdict on the spot: the drones had shown that they were not the makers, and the honey belonged to the bees.
lesson: When people argue over who deserves credit, ask each to show the work again. Those who did it are usually glad to, and those who did not find reasons to refuse.
people: Bees, drones, a wasp as judge
source: Phaedrus, Fables, Book III, 13 (Apes et Fuci Vespa Iudice)
